clue.text: Almost getting agreement about drink

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for agreement is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: nigh means nearly or almost
a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: Someone nearly reaching a deal over a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is an alcoholic drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Wintertime hazard for driver who's a learner?

blocks.note: Nov is the abbreviation for November, a cold month
ice on the road is a danger to motorists

explanation.surface: Wintry conditions endangering a motorist who has only just started driving.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one danger, but it splits into a month and a road hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a beginner, someone new to an activity and still being taught.

clue.text: Relatively old, but managing

blocks.note: first meaning: advancing in years
second meaning: coping, making progress

explanation.surface: Someone elderly but still coping fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both ageing, as in 'he's getting on a bit', and coping, as in 'how are you getting on?'

clue.text: Satellite dish rattles

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or wreck, so the following word's letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A satellite dish shaking in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Satellite dish looks like one phrase; satellite is the definition and dish the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Telstar was the 1962 communications satellite that relayed the first live transatlantic television pictures.

clue.text: Table showing some seasonal tariffs

indicators.note: showing some means only part of the following words is on display

blocks.note: runs across the two words

explanation.surface: A chart of holiday-season prices.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the table in a church at which communion is celebrated.

clue.text: Pretty semi-detached — wonderful little house

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word pretty is detached and kept

blocks.note: the first half of the six-letter word
fab is slang short for fabulous

explanation.surface: An estate agent gushing over a charming semi-detached home.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-detached looks like a kind of house, chiming with the definition, but it tells you to keep half of pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefab is a small factory-built dwelling, put up quickly in Britain after the war.

clue.text: Foreign food upset emperor and knight

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means set upside down, so the pair is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors
Sir is a knight's title

explanation.surface: An emperor and his knight put off their food by unfamiliar cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTO + SIR read upwards gives RIS-OTTO; Otto is also a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked in stock, so a food from abroad.

clue.text: Ruffle father badly

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Annoying one's father terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruffle looks like a verb, to annoy, but it is the noun for a gathered strip of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a gathered or pleated decorative strip of cloth, the same thing as a ruffle.

clue.text: Best man in love? On the contrary, infatuated

indicators.note: the opposite of the stated order: instead of the man being placed in love, love is placed in the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the shape of O
Ted is a man's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether the best man is in love, and answering that he is besotted.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary flips the literal instruction: love is not around the man, but goes inside the first word, with the man after.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted means foolishly smitten, completely taken with someone.

clue.text: Fish isnt changing colour across the Atlantic

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the preceding word alter their order

blocks.note: the fodder, its four letters rearranged
the American spelling of grey

explanation.surface: A fish whose colour does not alter when it crosses the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The stingray is a flat cartilaginous fish with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Description of women in demographic data

blocks.note: first meaning: bust, waist and hip measurements
second meaning: official figures on births, marriages and deaths

explanation.walkthrough: In the surface the phrase means a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements; literally it means population records.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a figure's chest, waist and hip sizes and government records of births, marriages and deaths.

clue.text: American animal taking credit for origin of litter

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it starts, its opening letter
one thing given for another is a swap, so the abbreviation takes the place of the selected letter

blocks.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
the opening letter, which is swapped out

explanation.surface: An American animal getting the blame for the litter scattered about.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LITTER, drop its opening L and put CR in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Critter is the American colloquial form of creature, used for any animal.

clue.text: Big charity show's over, having put out hard message

indicators.note: putting something out removes it, so the letter for hard is dropped
turned over means the remaining letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a long televised fundraising broadcast
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A big charity broadcast has finished, after a tough message was sent out.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is': the show is over, that is, reversed, once its H has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded card for writing a short message on, so it stands for the message itself.

clue.text: A fish repeatedly extracted food ingredient from seaweed

blocks.note: taken as written
the gar is a long-snouted fish
the pair A and fish is written a second time

explanation.surface: Something taken from a fish over and over, turned into a food product from seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: Repeatedly means writing the A-plus-fish chunk twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar-agar is a gelatinous substance obtained from red seaweed and used to set jellies and thicken food.

clue.text: Governor General carries bird home rejoicing

indicators.note: something carried is held within, so the governor's letters hold the rest

blocks.note: GG is the abbreviation for Governor General
a lory is a brightly coloured parrot
at home means in

explanation.surface: A colonial governor bringing a bird home and celebrating.
explanation.walkthrough: G-LORY IN-G: the bird and IN sit between the two Gs.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorying means exulting or taking great delight, a form of rejoicing.

clue.text: Invigorating air i found beyond Australia

blocks.note: Oz is the colloquial name for Australia
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A traveller finding bracing fresh air out past Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Beyond places the second piece after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is used loosely for fresh, bracing sea air, as at a seaside resort.

clue.text: Primate wants an organ designed to hold a note

indicators.note: designed means made to a new plan, so the letters of an organ are rearranged
holding something keeps it inside, so the note goes within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the fodder
ut is the old name for the first note of the scale, now doh

explanation.surface: An ape in need of a purpose-built organ that can sustain a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, and so a primate.

clue.text: He's beginning to study free-range farm hens

indicators.note: free-range things roam loose, so the following letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: A beginner taking up the study of free-range poultry farming.
explanation.walkthrough: Free-range belongs with the hens in the surface, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshman is a first-year student at college, so someone starting out at university.

clue.text: Farming concern removing head of local office

indicators.note: removing the head means the opening letter is cut away

blocks.note: a branch is a local office of a bank or firm

explanation.surface: An agricultural business closing down its local branch manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle, so it is an agricultural business.

clue.text: Person over the hill was made perfect

blocks.note: first meaning: someone past their prime
second meaning: the past tense of to be turned into the present perfect tense

explanation.walkthrough: Perfect is the grammar term: the present perfect of 'was' is the two-word form.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is someone once famous or successful whose best days are behind them.

clue.text: Ring's mainly involved with power of gods

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed together into a new order

blocks.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
taken as written, as part of the fodder
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An opera buff saying Wagner's Ring is mostly about the gods' power.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Ring suggests Wagner's opera cycle, and mainly looks like 'mostly', but it is anagram fodder; the definition is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Greek deities who lived on Mount Olympus, so it means belonging to them.

clue.text: Team-mate runs to catch up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
to entrap is to catch

explanation.surface: A teammate dashing to draw level with the others.
explanation.walkthrough: Catch up looks like one phrasal verb, but up is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a companion on the same side, as in doubles tennis or bridge.

clue.text: Another building appropriate to the east

blocks.note: to annex is to appropriate or seize
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An extra building suitably placed on the eastern side.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate reads as an adjective, suitable, but it is the verb to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extra building added to or near a main one.

clue.text: It's loud — talk about that, do

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes around the other pieces

blocks.note: to say is to speak or talk
'tis is the old contraction of it is
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A complaint that something is noisy, and a request to discuss it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tis is the poetic contraction of it is. Do is meant as in 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in the sense of 'that will do' means to be good enough, to meet a need or suffice.

clue.text: Raised starting price— routine for oil in short supply

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted up, so the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: SP is the racing abbreviation for starting price
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: Rising prices and routine rationing when oil is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: SP RUT read upwards gives TUR-PS. 'Oil in short' means oil abbreviated; supply is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Turps is the shortened form of turpentine, an oil distilled from pine resin.

clue.text: Quiet part of Spain is ideal

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
Aragon is a region in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A traveller declaring a peaceful corner of Spain perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example, a model of excellence, so it means an ideal as a noun.

clue.text: Cruise beginning in Peru - take a boat over lake

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter
to row is to propel a boat
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Starting a cruise in Peru by rowing across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Over places the pieces above the lake's letter in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cruise can mean to roam about looking for something, which is to prowl.

clue.text: I treat one in team differently — she lost her head in public

definitions.text: she lost her head in public

indicators.note: arranged differently means the given letters are put in another order

blocks.note: the fodder, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A coach handling one squad member differently, who then loses her temper in front of everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Lost her head means lost her temper in the surface, but literally she was beheaded in public in 1793.
explanation.definitionFit: The French queen was guillotined in front of a crowd in Paris during the Revolution.

clue.text: Sampling bouquet to find what's wrong in drink

indicators.note: in places the word for wrongdoing inside the word for the drink

blocks.note: nog is eggnog, or a strong ale
a sin is a wrong act

explanation.surface: A wine taster sniffing to find the fault in a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: NO-SIN-G: the wrong goes inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosing is the wine taster's term for smelling a wine to judge its aroma, its bouquet.

clue.text: Poet one's seen getting out of nice carriage

indicators.note: seen getting out of means spotted leaving, so the letter for one departs from the following word

blocks.note: John Clare was an English rural poet
Roman numeral one, the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet being spotted stepping down from a handsome carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: John Clare is the 19th-century Northamptonshire peasant poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn coach seating four, named after the Duke of Clarence.
